spike_verdict: The spike itself (steward-branded shareholder club charging $30-$40, banning walk-ons, challenged in 2021 over its own deed) reads clean post-repair — the v1 lawsuit/1952-pricing overstatements were correctly fixed — but two internal-consistency defects survive: a repair-introduced arithmetic slip in the history spoke's framing sentence, and a pullquote that misstates why the club hired a police officer in a way that contradicts the spoke's own body text.

blocking.claim: "Gooseberry Beach sits on land shaped by two separate disputes a century apart: an 1880 fight over Hazard's estate ... and a 2021 fight over what the public is entitled to ..."
blocking.problem: 1880 to 2021 is 141 years, not "a century apart." This is the v1-verify repair's own fix text (v1 flagged a false-equivalence problem and proposed this exact sentence) but the repair dropped the original page's correct hedge ("more than a century apart") when rewriting it, introducing a new arithmetic understatement — a reader would take '"a century" to mean roughly 100 years, not 141.
blocking.evidence: F08 (1880 Hazard death) and the 2021 timeline row (F26/F27); 2021 - 1880 = 141 years.
blocking.fix: "Gooseberry Beach sits on land shaped by two separate disputes a century and a half apart: an 1880 fight over Hazard's estate that determined who would own this stretch of coastline, and a 2021 fight over what the public is entitled to once inside that ownership."

blocking.claim: "A club that calls itself a steward of the beach still needed a police officer to keep people from just walking in."
blocking.problem: Misstates the sourced reason for the hire. F27 says the officer was hired to direct dangerous rideshare drop-off/pick-up traffic on a narrow, shoulderless Ocean Drive — a road-safety measure. The pullquote instead frames the officer's job as blocking pedestrian walk-on entry to the beach (access enforcement), which is exactly the causal link history.mdx explicitly rules out one section earlier: "The police officer the club hired to manage dangerous rideshare drop-off traffic on Ocean Drive is, per the only reporting on it, a response to a road-safety problem rather than the access dispute." A reader hitting only the pullquote would come away with the opposite of what the sourced reporting and the page's own deep-dive say.
blocking.evidence: F27: "gooseberry had to employ a police officer to help direct traffic" (rideshare drop-off/pick-up traffic, Ocean Drive); history.mdx: "is, per the only reporting on it, a response to a road-safety problem rather than the access dispute."
blocking.fix: "A club that calls itself a steward of the beach still needed a police officer just to keep rideshare traffic from stopping on its road."

advisory.where: composition/showcase.json timeline, row "2021-6: Resident threatens legal action over access"
advisory.claim: "A part-time resident retains a lawyer seeking public beach access under Gooseberry's 1952 deed; the club hires a police officer for dangerous rideshare traffic." (fact_ids F26, F27, one row/title)
advisory.problem: Bundling F26 (the legal threat) and F27 (the police-officer hire) into a single dated event under a title about the access dispute invites the same causal misread as the pullquote above — that the officer was a response to the legal threat — even though history.mdx and overview.mdx both correctly present the hire as an unrelated road-safety measure. Not blocking on its own (a timeline row juxtaposing two same-month facts is defensible), but it reinforces the pullquote's error rather than correcting it.
advisory.evidence: F26/F27, both Newport Buzz 2021-06; history.mdx: "is ... a response to a road-safety problem rather than the access dispute."
advisory.fix: Split into two rows, or reword the single row so causation isn't implied: "A part-time resident retains a lawyer seeking public beach access under Gooseberry's 1952 deed. Separately, rising rideshare traffic on Ocean Drive leads the club to hire a police officer for road safety."

advisory.fix: Either drop the quotation marks (paraphrase) or correct the text to "Exposed — real surf, and rip current to respect."
